title: Equal groups: multiplying and dividing
summary: Put apples into equal groups, build arrays and see how multiplying and dividing fit together.
guide: This studio covers Year 1–3 work on {{term:multiplication}} and {{term:division}}. Your child works with counters and answers by tapping a number.
Here 3 × 4 means "3 groups of 4", which is 4 + 4 + 4 ({{term:repeated-addition}}). A common slip is to add the two numbers (3 + 4 = 7).

Division has two meanings: sharing (share 12 apples between 3 plates: how many on each?) and grouping (put 15 counters into groups of 5: how many groups?). Both are answered by a multiplication fact: 3 × 5 = 15, so 15 ÷ 5 = 3.
Turning an array shows that 4 × 5 = 5 × 4 (the {{term:commutative-property}}), and splitting one shows that 4 × 7 = 4 × 5 + 4 × 2 (the {{term:distributive-property}}).

engine.instruction-split: Tap a counter to split the array in two.

equal-groups.title: 3 groups of 4
equal-groups.prompt: Maryam has 3 plates. She puts 4 apples on each plate. Put the apples on the plates. How many apples are on the plates altogether?
equal-groups.hint: The + button by each plate takes one apple from the basket. Each plate needs 4 apples. Then count in 4s: 4, 8, …
equal-groups.success: Well done! 3 groups of 4 make 12. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 and 3 × 4 = 12
equal-groups.model: Because 3 × 4 means 3 lots of 4, not 3 and 4. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Adding 3 and 4 only counts one plate and 3 more apples.

feedback.not-equal: The plates are not equal. Each plate needs 4 apples.
feedback.too-few: Each plate needs 4 apples. Put more on.
feedback.too-many: That's more than 4. Tap an apple to send it back to the basket.
feedback.added: You worked out 3 + 4. But there are 3 groups with 4 apples in each. Count all the apples on the plates.
feedback.one-group: That's the apples on one plate. There are three plates.
feedback.counted-groups: 3 is the number of plates. We want the number of apples.
feedback.basket: 15 is all the apples we started with. Count only the apples on the plates.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

build-array.title: Equal rows
build-array.prompt: Arrange the counters in 4 rows with 5 counters in each row. How many counters are there?
build-array.hint: Use + and − to change the number of rows, and the other + and − to change how many are in each row.
build-array.why: Press the turn button. Now you have 5 rows of 4. Why are there still 20 counters?
build-array.model: They are the same counters; we only turned the array. Rows became columns and columns became rows. So 4 × 5 = 5 × 4 = 20. This is the {{term:commutative-property}} of multiplication.

feedback.wrong-array: You need 4 rows with 5 counters in each. Count the rows.
feedback.added: You worked out 4 + 5. But there are 4 rows with 5 in each: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5.
feedback.one-row: That's just one row. Count all the rows.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

split-array.title: Split a multiplication
split-array.prompt: Here are 4 rows of 7. Don't know 4 × 7? Build it from facts you know. Split the array after the 5th column: 4 × 5 and 4 × 2. What is 4 × 7?
split-array.hint: Tap a counter in the 5th column. The red part is 4 × 5 and the yellow part is 4 × 2. Add them.
split-array.why: Why can we split 4 × 7 into two parts and add them?
split-array.model: No counters are lost and none are added. 7 = 5 + 2, so each row has 5 red and 2 yellow: 4 × 7 = 4 × 5 + 4 × 2. This is the {{term:distributive-property}}.

feedback.wrong-colors: Split the array after the 5th column: 5 red columns and 2 yellow ones.
feedback.split-added: You worked out 20 + 2. The yellow part isn't 2 counters; it is 4 rows of 2: 4 × 2 = 8.
feedback.too-big: Count the red part, then the yellow part, and add them.
feedback.too-small: Count the red part, then the yellow part, and add them.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

share.title: Sharing
share.prompt: Reza has 12 apples. He shares them equally between 3 plates. Share them one at a time until the basket is empty. How many apples are on each plate?
share.hint: Tap the + buttons in turn: plate 1, plate 2, plate 3, plate 1 again, …
share.success: Well done! Each plate has 4 apples. 12 ÷ 3 = 4
share.why: How can a multiplication show that your answer is right?
share.model: There are 3 plates with 4 apples on each: 3 × 4 = 12. That's the 12 apples we started with, so 12 ÷ 3 = 4 is right. Multiplying and dividing undo each other.

feedback.too-many: There are still apples in the basket. Finish sharing.
feedback.not-equal: The plates are not equal. Take an apple off the fullest plate (tap it to send it back).
feedback.plates: 3 is the number of plates. Count the apples on one plate.
feedback.total: 12 is all the apples. Count the apples on one plate.
feedback.subtracted: You worked out 12 − 3. But we shared the apples; we didn't take any away.
feedback.too-big: Count the apples on one plate again.
feedback.too-small: Count the apples on one plate again.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

groups-of-five.title: Groups of 5
groups-of-five.prompt: There are 15 counters. Put them in rows of 5. How many rows of 5 are there?
groups-of-five.hint: Use + to make each row longer until it holds 5. Then count the rows.
groups-of-five.why: Using 3, 5 and 15, what other multiplication and division facts can you write?
groups-of-five.model: 3 × 5 = 15, 5 × 3 = 15, 15 ÷ 5 = 3 and 15 ÷ 3 = 5. All four are about the same 15 counters: 3 rows of 5, or 5 columns of 3. This is a fact family.

feedback.wrong-array: Each row needs 5 counters. Count the counters in the first row.
feedback.group-size: 5 is how many are in each row. We want the number of rows.
feedback.subtracted: You worked out 15 − 5. Find how many 5s fit into 15.
feedback.total: 15 is all the counters. Count the rows.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.
